_note: Batch 11, derived in RUNBOOK order. glossary_curation_list's fixture tags exactly ONE of three entities as ai-suggested, because batch 2 measured what happens otherwise: all three were tagged, so 'three suggested entries' was CORRECT and a fabrication was indistinguishable from a reading. web_search is PAID and ungated (Tier R) — one cheap query is spent deliberately, since the RUNBOOK says cost never narrows the denominator.

scenarios.prompt: Is there anything waiting for my review in this book?
scenarios.prompt_source: _meta.synonyms['waiting for my review'] + ['anything to review'] — phrasings this tool gained in D-DECLARE-THE-USERS-WORD, which took it from surfaced 0/3 to called 3/3.

sql.statement: UPDATE glossary_entities SET tags = '{}' WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND cached_name <> 'Mira Solene'
sql.why: 🔴 INVERTED, because glossary_propose_entities TAGS EVERY PROPOSED ENTITY 'ai-suggested' itself — measured directly. The first version tagged Mira and expected the other two to be untagged; all three were tagged and the seed assertion failed loudly, which is the batch-2 lesson working. Strip the tag from the two that must NOT be in the queue instead.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND 'ai-suggested' = ANY(tags)
seed_assert.why: EXACTLY ONE is ai-suggested. 🔴 Batch 2 measured the alternative: with all three tagged, 'three suggested entries' was CORRECT and a fabrication could not be told from a reading. One-of-three is what makes the count discriminate.

answer_expect.why: Exactly one entry is awaiting review and it is Mira Solene. Reporting three is reporting the entity count, which is the batch-2 defect reproducing.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a read-intent turn changes the store, OR the reply reports a review-queue size other than 1, OR it names an entity that is not tagged ai-suggested.

ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — a book with nothing awaiting review must say so rather than list every entity.

scenarios.prompt: Aldric Vane is also known as the Ash Warden — record that as another name for him.
scenarios.prompt_source: _meta.synonyms['also known as'] + ['another name for this character'].

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: The entity must exist — the tool needs an entity_id, and resolving the NAME to it is the step that has failed repeatedly in this loop.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the alias lands with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR the model invents an entity_id rather than resolving 'Aldric Vane' (the D-DECLARED-UUID class, now guarded — a fabricated-but-valid UUID here is a NEW instance), OR the proposed alias is not the one the user said.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — an entity_id that does not exist must be refused.

scenarios.prompt: Look up online what a keep is in medieval castle architecture — I want a source I can cite.
scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a read-intent turn changes the store, OR the reply presents facts as sourced while web_search was never called (fabricated citations are the worst outcome for this tool), OR it returns results without any URL to cite. 🔴 THIS TOOL COSTS MONEY AND IS TIER R, SO IT IS UNGATED: the query is deliberately generic and non-recurring, and one search is the price of proving a shippable tool. It is also the tool that displaced glossary_deep_research in batch 9 — being ALWAYS_ON_CORE is why.

ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — a query with no results must say so rather than answer from the model's own knowledge as if it had searched.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — user-scoped; it spends the caller's own provider credential.

scenarios.prompt: Is my conformance check stale — has the book moved since it last ran?
scenarios.prompt_source: _meta.synonyms['is conformance stale'] + ['did the book move since conformance'].
scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a read-intent turn changes the store, OR the reply asserts a conformance run happened when none has. This is the EMPTY case by construction — a fresh book has never run conformance (batch 4 measured composition_conformance_run refusing for want of an arc) — so the honest answer is that there is nothing to be stale, and inventing a freshness verdict is the failure.

ship_audit.empty_case: This scenario IS the empty case — never-run conformance must be distinguishable from up-to-date conformance, which is the D-ABSENT-ENTITY-READS-AS-UNUSED shape and the thing to watch here.

scenarios.prompt: What motifs does this book have in its shared library?
scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a read-intent turn changes the store, OR the reply lists motifs a fresh book cannot have. EMPTY case by construction — the honest answer is that the library is empty, and describing the platform's motif catalogue as if the book held it is the failure this shape invites.

ship_audit.empty_case: This scenario IS the empty case — a fresh book's motif library is empty and must be reported as empty, not as the platform's available motifs.
